resource.name: aws_mskconnect_connector
resource.description: Provides an Amazon MSK Connect Connector resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_mskconnect_connector` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of Amazon MSK Connect connectors, facilitating seamless integration between Apache Kafka clusters and external systems or data sources. Common use cases include setting up data pipelines for real-time streaming, connecting Kafka topics to databases, cloud services, or analytics platforms, and automating connector lifecycle management. Users can configure key aspects such as connector plugins, worker configurations, logging settings, and source or sink integration parameters to optimize data flow and processing.

examples.title: Basic configuration
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource, showcasing how to set up an MSK Connect connector with autoscaling capacity, custom plugin integration, and Apache Kafka cluster connectivity. It includes key configurations such as autoscaling policies, connector settings, VPC networking, encryption in transit, and IAM role association for service execution.

arguments.name: connector_configuration
arguments.description: (Required) A map of keys to values that represent the configuration for the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `connector_configuration` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define key-value pairs that configure the operational behavior and settings of the MSK Connect connector, such as source or sink properties, data transformation rules, or connection parameters. By specifying this required map, users can tailor the connector's functionality to integrate with external systems, control data flow, and meet specific application requirements.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) A summary description of the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define a human-readable summary that provides context or details about the connector's purpose or functionality. Setting this argument helps document the connector's role within the infrastructure, aiding in organization, clarity, and collaboration, especially in environments with multiple connectors.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource represents the unique identifier of the connector, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While optional, specifying this argument can be useful for referencing or managing the connector in Terraform configurations, enabling users to track and interact with the resource programmatically.

arguments.name: kafkaconnect_version
arguments.description: (Required) The version of Kafka Connect. It has to be compatible with both the Apache Kafka cluster's version and the plugins.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kafkaconnect_version` argument specifies the version of Kafka Connect to be used by the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource, ensuring compatibility with the Apache Kafka cluster and associated plugins. Setting this argument allows users to define the runtime environment for their connector, aligning it with the desired Kafka ecosystem version to enable seamless data streaming and integration functionality.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies the unique identifier for the connector, allowing users to define a human-readable name that distinguishes the connector within the MSK Connect environment. Setting this argument is essential for resource identification, organization, and management, aligning with common user goals like naming infrastructure components for clarity and operational tracking.

arguments.name: service_execution_role_arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role used by the connector to access the Amazon Web Services resources that it needs. The types of resources depends on the logic of the connector. For example, a connector that has Amazon S3 as a destination must have permissions that allow it to write to the S3 destination bucket. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `service_execution_role_arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants the `aws_mskconnect_connector` access to required AWS resources, such as S3 buckets or other services, based on the connector's logic and destination configuration. Setting this argument ensures the connector has the necessary permissions to perform its operations, enabling seamless integration with AWS services and secure execution of tasks.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the connector, enabling resource categorization, organization, and cost tracking. By defining tags, users can streamline management tasks such as identifying resources by environment, project, or ownership, while also integrating with AWS tagging-based features like billing and access control.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the connector and inherited from the provider-level default tags. This enables streamlined resource organization, cost allocation, and metadata management across AWS services, supporting common user goals like tagging for billing, access control, and resource categorization.

blocks.name: capacity
blocks.description: (Required) Information about the capacity allocated to the connector. See `capacity` Block for details.

blocks.name: autoscaling
blocks.description: (Optional) Information about the auto scaling parameters for the connector. See `autoscaling` Block for details.

arguments.name: max_worker_count
arguments.description: (Required) The maximum number of workers allocated to the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_worker_count` argument defines the upper limit on the number of workers that can be allocated to an MSK Connect connector, enabling users to control the scalability and resource utilization of the connector during autoscaling. By specifying this value, users ensure the connector can handle increased workloads while preventing over-allocation of resources, aligning with performance and cost optimization goals.

arguments.name: mcu_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of microcontroller units (MCUs) allocated to each connector worker. Valid values: `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`. The default value is `1`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `mcu_count` argument in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define the number of microcontroller units (MCUs) allocated to each connector worker, directly influencing the processing capacity and scalability of the connector. By configuring this value, users can optimize resource allocation for autoscaling scenarios, balancing performance and cost based on workload demands.

arguments.name: min_worker_count
arguments.description: (Required) The minimum number of workers allocated to the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_worker_count` argument specifies the minimum number of worker instances allocated to an MSK Connect connector, ensuring baseline capacity for processing data streams. This required setting directly controls the autoscaling behavior by defining the lower limit of resources, helping users maintain consistent performance and avoid under-provisioning in dynamic workloads.

blocks.name: scale_in_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) The scale-in policy for the connector. See `scale_in_policy` Block for details.

arguments.name: cpu_utilization_percentage
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies the CPU utilization percentage threshold at which you want connector scale in to be triggered.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the CPU utilization threshold (as a percentage) that triggers scale-in actions for the connector, allowing users to optimize resource usage and reduce costs by automatically decreasing capacity when CPU demand falls below the specified level. This argument is central to configuring the connector's adaptive scaling behavior within the "scale_in_policy."

blocks.llm_summary: The `scale_in_policy` block within the `autoscaling` context of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the rules and thresholds for reducing the number of connector instances during periods of decreased demand. By configuring this block, users can optimize resource utilization and cost efficiency by automating the scale-in process based on predefined metrics or conditions.

blocks.name: scale_out_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) The scale-out policy for the connector. See `scale_out_policy` Block for details.

arguments.name: cpu_utilization_percentage
arguments.description: (Required) The CPU utilization percentage threshold at which you want connector scale out to be triggered.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the CPU utilization threshold that triggers automatic scale-out for the connector, enabling dynamic resource allocation to handle increased workloads. This argument allows users to optimize performance and ensure scalability by specifying when additional capacity should be provisioned based on CPU usage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `scale_out_policy` block within the `autoscaling` context of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the rules and thresholds for automatically increasing the connector's capacity in response to workload demands. By configuring this block, users can optimize performance and ensure scalability by specifying conditions under which the connector scales out, enabling efficient resource utilization during peak loads.

The `autoscaling` block within the `capacity` configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines parameters for dynamically adjusting the connector's capacity based on workload demands. It encapsulates settings related to scaling policies and thresholds, enabling users to optimize resource utilization and ensure performance stability by automating capacity adjustments in response to traffic or processing needs.

blocks.name: provisioned_capacity
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about a fixed capacity allocated to a connector. See `provisioned_capacity` Block for details.

arguments.name: mcu_count
arguments.description: (Optional) The number of microcontroller units (MCUs) allocated to each connector worker. Valid values: `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`. The default value is `1`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `mcu_count` argument in the `provisioned_capacity` block of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define the number of microcontroller units (MCUs) allocated to each connector worker, directly influencing the processing capacity and performance of the connector. By configuring this value (e.g., `1`, `2`, `4`, or `8`), users can optimize resource allocation to meet workload demands, balancing cost and performance for their managed Kafka Connect infrastructure.

arguments.name: worker_count
arguments.description: (Required) The number of workers that are allocated to the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `worker_count` argument specifies the number of workers allocated to the MSK Connect connector, directly controlling the processing capacity and scalability of the connector within the `provisioned_capacity` configuration. By defining this value, users can ensure the connector has sufficient resources to handle data throughput and workload demands, aligning with performance and operational goals.

blocks.llm_summary: The `provisioned_capacity` block within the `capacity` configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines a fixed allocation of compute and memory resources for the connector, ensuring predictable performance and scalability. This block enables users to specify resource limits for connectors, providing fine-grained control over capacity planning to optimize workloads and maintain consistent operational efficiency.

The `capacity` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the allocation of computational and storage resources for the connector, enabling users to optimize performance and scalability based on workload requirements. This block encapsulates settings related to resource provisioning, such as memory, CPU, or throughput, allowing users to tailor the connector's capacity to efficiently handle data streaming tasks in Amazon MSK Connect.

blocks.name: kafka_cluster
blocks.description: (Required) Specifies which Apache Kafka cluster to connect to. See `kafka_cluster` Block for details.

blocks.name: apache_kafka_cluster
blocks.description: (Required) The Apache Kafka cluster to which the connector is connected. See `apache_kafka_cluster` Block for details.

arguments.name: bootstrap_servers
arguments.description: (Required) The bootstrap servers of the cluster.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bootstrap_servers` argument specifies the connection endpoints (host:port pairs) for the Apache Kafka cluster that the MSK Connect connector will interact with. By defining this required parameter, users establish the communication link between the connector and the Kafka cluster, enabling the connector to produce or consume data streams as part of the integration workflow.

blocks.name: vpc
blocks.description: (Required) Details of an Amazon VPC which has network connectivity to the Apache Kafka cluster. See `vpc` Block for details.

arguments.name: security_groups
arguments.description: (Required) The security groups for the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the set of security groups that control inbound and outbound traffic for the AWS MSK Connect connector within the VPC, ensuring network-level access restrictions and enabling secure communication with other resources. This argument is essential for configuring the connector's network isolation and compliance with security best practices.

arguments.name: subnets
arguments.description: (Required) The subnets for the connector.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnets` argument specifies the set of VPC subnets where the MSK Connect connector will be deployed, ensuring network connectivity and isolation within the defined private infrastructure. By configuring this required parameter, users control the connector's placement within the VPC, enabling secure communication with other resources and services while adhering to subnet-specific routing and access policies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `vpc` configuration block for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the Amazon VPC settings required to establish network connectivity between the MSK Connect connector and the Apache Kafka cluster. It encapsulates related settings such as subnets and security groups, enabling users to securely integrate the connector with Kafka while ensuring proper network isolation and access control. Configuring this block is essential for achieving seamless communication and secure data flow within a private cloud environment.

The `apache_kafka_cluster` configuration block defines the connection details for the Apache Kafka cluster that the MSK Connect connector interacts with, enabling seamless integration between the connector and the Kafka cluster. It encapsulates settings related to cluster identification and connectivity, ensuring the connector can reliably produce or consume data streams. Configuring this block allows users to establish and manage the connector's communication with a specific Kafka cluster, facilitating data pipeline operations and stream processing workflows.

The `kafka_cluster` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies the Apache Kafka cluster that the connector will interact with, enabling seamless integration with a target Kafka environment. It encapsulates settings required to define the connection to the Kafka cluster, such as cluster details and access configurations, allowing users to establish and manage connectivity to their Kafka infrastructure for data streaming and processing workflows.

blocks.name: kafka_cluster_client_authentication
blocks.description: (Required) Details of the client authentication used by the Apache Kafka cluster. See `kafka_cluster_client_authentication` Block for details.

arguments.name: authentication_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of client authentication used to connect to the Apache Kafka cluster. Valid values: `IAM`, `NONE`. A value of `NONE` means that no client authentication is used. The default value is `NONE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `authentication_type` argument in the `kafka_cluster_client_authentication` block of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to specify the method of client authentication for connecting to an Apache Kafka cluster. By setting this argument to `IAM` or `NONE`, users can control whether authentication is enforced (via AWS IAM) or disabled, impacting the security model and access control for Kafka cluster connections.

blocks.llm_summary: The `kafka_cluster_client_authentication` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the client authentication mechanism for securely connecting to an Apache Kafka cluster. It encapsulates settings related to authentication protocols, such as SASL or TLS, enabling users to configure secure access and ensure compliance with security requirements for Kafka data streaming workflows.

blocks.name: kafka_cluster_encryption_in_transit
blocks.description: (Required) Details of encryption in transit to the Apache Kafka cluster. See `kafka_cluster_encryption_in_transit` Block for details.

arguments.name: encryption_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of encryption in transit to the Apache Kafka cluster. Valid values: `PLAINTEXT`, `TLS`. The default values is `PLAINTEXT`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encryption_type` argument for the `kafka_cluster_encryption_in_transit` configuration in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to specify the level of encryption applied to data transmitted between the connector and the Apache Kafka cluster. By setting this argument to either `PLAINTEXT` or `TLS`, users can control whether communication is unencrypted or secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS), aligning with security requirements for data in transit.

blocks.llm_summary: The `kafka_cluster_encryption_in_transit` block within the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource configures encryption settings for data transmitted between the MSK Connect connector and the Apache Kafka cluster. It ensures secure communication by defining encryption protocols, enabling users to protect sensitive data in transit and comply with security best practices for Kafka-based integrations.

blocks.name: log_delivery
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about log delivery. See `log_delivery` Block for details.

blocks.name: worker_log_delivery
blocks.description: (Required) The workers can send worker logs to different destination types. This configuration specifies the details of these destinations. See `worker_log_delivery` Block for details.

blocks.name: cloudwatch_logs
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about delivering logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. See `cloudwatch_logs` Block for details.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs is enabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument for the `cloudwatch_logs` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies whether Amazon CloudWatch Logs integration is activated for the connector. Setting this to `true` enables log delivery to CloudWatch Logs, allowing users to monitor, troubleshoot, and analyze connector activity, which is essential for operational visibility and debugging.

arguments.name: log_group
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the CloudWatch log group that is the destination for log delivery.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_group` argument for the `cloudwatch_logs` configuration in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to specify the name of the CloudWatch log group where connector logs will be delivered. By defining this, users can centralize and monitor connector activity, enabling log analysis, troubleshooting, and compliance tracking within their AWS environment.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cloudwatch_logs` block within the `worker_log_delivery` configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource enables delivery of worker logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for centralized monitoring and troubleshooting. It encapsulates settings related to log stream and log group configuration, allowing users to efficiently track connector activity, diagnose issues, and maintain operational visibility.

blocks.name: firehose
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about delivering logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. See `firehose` Block for details.

arguments.name: delivery_stream
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that is the destination for log delivery.
arguments.llm_summary: The `delivery_stream` argument allows users to specify the name of a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to serve as the destination for log delivery from the MSK Connect connector. Configuring this argument enables centralized log management and monitoring by directing connector logs to a Firehose stream for further processing, storage, or integration with analytics tools.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies whether connector logs get delivered to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument for the `firehose` configuration in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies whether connector logs are delivered to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Setting this argument to `true` enables log delivery, allowing users to capture, process, and analyze connector logs for monitoring, debugging, or compliance purposes.

blocks.llm_summary: The `firehose` configuration block within the `worker_log_delivery` context of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the settings for delivering worker logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. This block enables users to configure log delivery mechanisms, facilitating centralized log management and real-time analytics by integrating with Firehose as a destination for processing and storing logs.

blocks.name: s3
blocks.description: (Optional) Details about delivering logs to Amazon S3. See `s3` Block for deetails.

arguments.name: bucket
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the S3 bucket that is the destination for log delivery.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the name of the S3 bucket where MSK Connect logs are delivered, enabling users to configure log storage for monitoring, auditing, or troubleshooting purposes. This argument allows users to specify the destination for log delivery, supporting common goals like centralized log management and integration with other AWS services for analysis or retention.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies whether connector logs get sent to the specified Amazon S3 destination.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled` argument for the `s3` configuration in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies whether connector logs are sent to an Amazon S3 destination. Setting this required boolean to `true` enables log delivery to S3, allowing users to configure centralized log storage for monitoring, auditing, or troubleshooting purposes.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) The S3 prefix that is the destination for log delivery.
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix` argument in the `s3` context of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define a custom S3 key prefix for organizing and specifying the destination path of log delivery within the S3 bucket. By setting this optional string, users can control how logs are structured and stored, enabling better organization, retrieval, and management of log data for their MSK Connect connectors.

blocks.llm_summary: The `s3` configuration block within the `worker_log_delivery` context of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource enables the delivery of worker logs to Amazon S3 for centralized storage and analysis. It encapsulates settings related to S3 bucket details, access permissions, and log delivery configurations, allowing users to efficiently manage and persist logs for auditing, troubleshooting, or compliance purposes.

The `worker_log_delivery` block within the `log_delivery` configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines how worker logs are delivered to specific destinations, such as Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. This block enables users to configure detailed log delivery settings, ensuring centralized log management and monitoring for MSK Connect worker processes.

The `log_delivery` configuration block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource enables the setup and management of log delivery mechanisms for the connector, allowing users to define how logs are captured and stored. This block encapsulates settings related to log destinations, such as Amazon S3 or CloudWatch Logs, helping users achieve centralized logging and monitoring for troubleshooting, auditing, and performance analysis of their MSK Connect connectors.

blocks.name: plugin
blocks.description: (Required) Specifies which plugins to use for the connector. See `plugin` Block for details.

blocks.name: custom_plugin
blocks.description: (Required) Details about a custom plugin. See `custom_plugin` Block for details.

arguments.name: arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the custom plugin.
arguments.llm_summary: The `arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the custom plugin to be used by the MSK Connect connector, enabling users to integrate and configure custom processing logic or transformations for Kafka data streams. By defining this required parameter, users ensure the connector leverages the desired plugin, aligning with specific data processing or enrichment goals.

arguments.name: revision
arguments.description: (Required) The revision of the custom plugin.
arguments.llm_summary: The `revision` argument specifies the version of the custom plugin to be used with the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource, allowing users to control which iteration of the plugin is deployed. Setting this argument ensures compatibility and enables users to manage updates or rollbacks to specific plugin revisions for their MSK Connect connector configuration.

blocks.llm_summary: The `custom_plugin` block within the `plugin` configuration of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the details required to use a custom plugin with the MSK Connect connector. It encapsulates settings for specifying and managing the custom plugin's source, version, and deployment, enabling users to integrate custom-built functionality or third-party extensions into their MSK Connect workflows for enhanced data streaming capabilities.

The `plugin` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines the plugins to be used by the MSK Connect connector, enabling users to specify and configure the necessary components for data transformation, integration, or custom processing within the connector pipeline. This block allows for precise control over the connector's functionality by encapsulating plugin-specific settings, ensuring compatibility and tailored behavior for the desired use case.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (in string format, e.g., "10m" for 10 minutes) Terraform should wait for the connector creation process to complete. By configuring this timeout, users can control the lifecycle behavior of the resource, ensuring operations do not hang indefinitely and align with deployment expectations for MSK Connect connectors.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (in string format) Terraform should wait for the connector to be deleted during a resource lifecycle operation. Configuring this timeout ensures predictable behavior during deletion, helping users manage resource cleanup efficiently and avoid prolonged operations or potential timeouts in their infrastructure workflows.

arguments.name: update
arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource allows users to define the maximum duration Terraform will wait for an update operation to complete on the MSK Connect connector. By configuring this timeout, users can ensure smoother lifecycle management of the connector, particularly in scenarios where updates may take longer due to resource constraints or complex configurations.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource defines customizable time limits for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting an MSK Connect connector. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent long-running tasks from exceeding acceptable thresholds, ensuring better control over resource lifecycle management and operational efficiency.

blocks.name: worker_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Specifies which worker configuration to use with the connector. See `worker_configuration` Block for details.

arguments.name: arn
arguments.description: (Required) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the worker configuration.
arguments.llm_summary: The `arn` argument specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the worker configuration for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource, allowing users to define the operational settings and runtime parameters for the connector's worker nodes. By setting this value, users ensure the connector leverages a predefined worker configuration, which typically impacts resource allocation, performance tuning, and compatibility with Kafka workloads.

arguments.name: revision
arguments.description: (Required) The revision of the worker configuration.
arguments.llm_summary: The `revision` argument specifies the version of the worker configuration to be used for the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource, allowing users to control which iteration of the configuration is applied to the connector's runtime environment. Setting this argument ensures the connector operates with the desired configuration updates, enabling precise management of worker behavior and compatibility with evolving application requirements.

blocks.llm_summary: The `worker_configuration` block in the `aws_mskconnect_connector` resource specifies the worker configuration settings used to manage the operational behavior of the connector, including runtime parameters and resource allocation. Configuring this block allows users to define and associate a specific worker configuration, enabling fine-grained control over connector performance and compatibility with MSK Connect workloads.
